Commercial poultry farming (i.e., commercial use) shall be done in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local law, including the following:

- (a) District: Commercial poultry farming is permitted exclusively in land zoned for the forestry-agricultural district.

- (b) Enclosures: Poultry shall be kept in enclosed structures that include a roof, door, and proper ventilation (e.g., chicken houses). Ventilation for these enclosures shall be directed away from any residence on adjacent property. Poultry are only permitted to roam within a yard connected to their enclosure which is also enclosed, either by fences or walls at least six (6) feet in height; or alternatively, by fences or walls at least four (4) feet in height which are covered by a roof. Poultry are not permitted to roam outside of their enclosure or yard onto adjacent property or into any public road or right-of-way. Construction of all enclosures, yards, fences, and other structures pertinent to commercial poultry farming shall be performed to minimize thelr impact on or any nuisance to adjacent property owners.

- (c) Location and boundaries: Any enclosure must be located at least: two hundred (200) feet from the property lines or any water source; five hundred (500) feet from any residence on adjacent property; and one thousand two hundred (1,200) feet from any church, school, or place of business. These boundaries may be waived only by consent of the owners of the adjacent property, church, school, or place of business. Such waiver does not permit the roaming of any poultry outside of their enclosures.

- (d) Vegetative buffer/barrier. Any property engaged in commercial poultry farming that is adjacent to properties in any other district (including but not limited to rural residential, suburban residential, urban residential, and scenic corridor districts) shall plant and maintain a vegetative buffer or barrier and Include plans for the same as part of its site plan and permit application. Landscaping within buffer areas shall be used to screen objectionable views or nuisances, including without limitation any parking and service areas, refuse containers, air conditioning units and transformers. The Administrator may waive or modify the requirements for a vegetative buffer where a sufficient land barrier (e.g., hill) or man-made barrier (e.g., fence or wall) exists that accomplishes the same purpose as the vegetative buffer.

- 1. Dimensions: The buffer shall extend along the entire portion of the property line abutting the commercial poultry facilities plus fifty (50) feet in each direction beyond the facilities. The plantings on the buffer shall consist of evergreen trees or shrubs with an initial height of at least four (4) feet in height and which will eventually achieve at least eight (8) feet in height. Existing on-site trees may be credited as meeting the requirements of this article if the Administrator determines that such plant materials achieve the purposes of this article.

- 2. Location of buffers: Buffers shall be located on the outer perimeter of a lot or parcel along all lot lines adjoining dissimilar districts including adjacent property lines, which may be separated by an existing or proposed public right-of-way. Buffers shall not be located on any portion of existing, dedicated, or reserved public or private road or right-of-way.

- 3. Maintenance of buffers: The responsibility for maintenance of buffers shall remain with the landowner and shall include prompt replacement of any portion of the vegetative buffer that has died or otherwise must be replaced to serve its intended purpose. Maintenance of planted areas shall include mowing, removal of litter and dead plant materials, and necessary pruning. Fences and walls shall be kept In a condition that meets the requirements of this article.

- 4. Site plan: Prior to development, a site plan shall be required to show the types and locations of all plantings within a required buffer.

- (e) Processing: Processing of poultry for meat is prohibited on property with commercial poultry houses.

- (f) Waste, sanitation, and litter.

- 1. Waste: All waste produced by poultry other than litter is categorized as industrial waste or by-product, as defined in Sec. 2.1, and shall be stored on-site for no more than seventy-two (72) hours in water-tight, sealable containers on a concrete base which fully accommodates the dimensions of the containers. Storage of industrial waste or by-product exceeding twelve (72) hours is restricted to industrial districts. Disposal of industrial waste or by-product shall be done in conformity with applicable law. Any person generating, storing, or transporting any industrial waste or by-product shall be llable for any leaks, spills, or exposure which result in contamination, property damage, or personal injury, including death.

Industrial waste storage shall occur as follows: at least two hundred (200) feet from the property lines or any water source; at least five hundred (500) feet from any residence on adjacent property; at least one thousand two hundred (1,200) feet from any church, school, or place of business. These boundaries may be waived only by the advanced written consent of the owner(s) of the adjacent property, church, school, or place of business.

- 2. Carcasses: All unprocessed poultry carcasses shail be disposed of in accordance with Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 40-13-10 via a pit, incinerator, or other means explicitly approved in writing by the Georgia Department of Agriculture.

- 3. Sanitation: All waste either produced by poultry or from processing poultry which is found in any open-air area, enclosure, exterior premise, or interior premise shall be removed within twelve (12) hours. Enclosures must include proper drainage and remain dry, with properly functioning ventilation and drinking systems. Exterior walls, fences, and roofs of enclosures, yards, or processing structures, along with all coops and cages, must remain clean of all waste, stains, or other residue, per Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 40-13-10-.06.

Litter: Poultry litter that is not being recycled per a nutrient management plan (NMP) or other waste management process approved by the relevant state or federal agency shall be disposed at a sanitary landfill or, alternatively, used or sold for use as organic fertilizer or in some other manner consistent with generally accepted agricultural practices.

- (g) Breeding: Breeding poultry to produce additional poultry rather than sterilized eggs for commercial sale is subject to the permit costs in subsection (h) and Table 5.6.5 below.

- (h) Permit Required: Use of land for commercial poultry farming is conditioned upon a commercial poultry permit. This permit may be granted by the Administrator upon review and approval of the application, which shall include the following:

1.

The applicant shall produce a copy of all relevant licenses, either state or federal, pertaining to commercial agriculture or poultry farming.

The applicant shall produce documentation of their compliance with rules and requirements of the Georgia Poultry Improvement Association (GPIA), as the official state agency of the National Poultry Improvement Plan (NPIP) created by the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), per O.C.G.A. § 4-7-1 et seg. This includes any requirements for shipping poultry either to or from Georgia as well as on-site sanitation, vaccination, and testing requirements for poultry.

The applicant shall produce their certificate from the Commissioner of the Department of Agriculture approving their proposed means of poultry carcass disposal in accordance with Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 40-13-10, whether by pit, incinerator, or another means explicitly approved by the Department of Agriculture in writing.

The applicant shall produce their nutrient management plan (NMP) outlining their management of litter and safeguards against contamination of surface or ground waters as well as other environmental hazards.

The applicant shall produce a copy of the registration of their Confined Animal Feeding Operation (CAFO) with the relevant state or federal agency, including but not limited to the Georgia Environmental Protection Division (EPD), the Georgia Department of Agriculture (GDOA), or the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

. Commercial Poultry Farming Plan: The applicant shall produce a “Commercial

Poultry Farming Plan” which includes (i) the plat and address for the property where the farm shall be built, including a depiction of all adjacent property and water sources; (ii) the estimated number of poultry birds to be housed at any given time; (iii} the dimensions, construction, and locations of the enclosure(s) for housing the poultry; (iv) the dimensions, construction, and locations of any connected yards, as well as fences, walls, and roofs; (v) the dimensions, construction, and locations of waste storage for both industrial and non-industrial waste; and (vi) the location and contents of any vegetative buffers required by this article.

- 7. Site Visit: The applicant shall accompany the Administrator on a site visit of the proposed commercial poultry farm. The officer shall review the “Commercial Poultry Farming Plan” and confirm that the proposed site corresponds to the plan and does not violate any of the zoning boundaries listed in this Section.

- 8. Permit Cost: The annual cost for a permit shall depend on the total capacity of poultry houses of the applicant, regardless of whether such capacity Is utilized, and is detailed in Table 5.6.5 below. The permit fee is payable to the Administrator. Increasing the amount of pouitry birds in an existing commercial farm with an existing permit shall require payment of the balance on the appropriate fee.

- 9. Permit Term: Each commercial poultry permit shall be valid for one (1) year. The applicant may renew their permit by paying the applicable fee and accompanying the Administrator on an inspection to ensure that all applicable zoning boundaries are being observed.

- 10. Failure to satisfy one or more of the application requirements shall result in denial of the permit.

- (i) Nuisance: A nuisance, as defined in Sec. 2.1, may occur even when there is compliance with other applicable law, Including this ordinance. The Administrator may determine what conduct is necessary for abatement, including but not limited to changing the locations and boundaries of enclosures and waste storage as well as modifying sanitation practices and schedules. Failure to abate a nuisance as required by the Administrator may result in revocation of the commercial poultry permit in addition to other penalties and remedies under existing law.

Non-commercial poultry farming {i.6., non-commercial use) shall be done in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local law, including the following:

- (a) Districts: Non-commercial poultry farming and ownership is permitted exclusively in land zoned for the conservation district, forestry-agricultural district, rural residential district, and suburban residential district.

- (b) Enclosures: Poultry shall be provided an enclosed structure that includes a roof, door, and proper ventilation (6.g., chicken coop). Mechanical ventilation for these enclosures shall be directed away from any residence on adjacent property. Poultry are only permitted to roam within a yard connected to their enclosure which is also enclosed, either by fences or walls at least six (6) feet in height; or alternatively, by fences or walls

Pets may be kept inside the owner's residence or an enclosed yard meeting the same requirements detailed In thls subsection.

- (c) Location and boundaries: Any enclosure must be located at least two hundred (200) feet from the property lines or any water source; and three hundred (300) feet from any residence on adjacent property. These boundaries may be waived only by consent of the owners of the adjacent property. Such waiver does not permit the roaming of any poultry outside of their enclosures or yards.

- (d) Processing: All processing of poultry for meat shall occur in an enclosed structure including a roof and door with proper ventilation directed away from residences on any adjacent property. Processing shall occur with the same boundaries and conditions as subsection {c).

- (e) Waste storage, disposal, and sanitation:

- 1. Waste: All waste produced by poultry other than litter is categorized as Industrial waste or by-product, as defined in Sec. 2.1, and shall be stored on-site in any water-tight, sealable container(s) on a concrete base which fully accommodates the dimensions of the container(s). All non-litter waste from processing poultry (e.g., blood, bones, offal) shall be stored in the same or a similar container(s). Waste shall be disposed of at a sanitary landfill within two (2) weeks of its original storage or in accordance with another waste management process approved by the relevant state or federal authority.

Waste storage must occur pursuant to the same boundaries and conditions as subsection (c) of this Section.

- 2. Carcasses: Poultry carcass disposal shall occur in compliance with Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 40-13-10 by using either a pit, incinerator, or other mean explicitly approved by the Department of Agriculture in writing, with the exception that pets may be buried or cremated.

- 3. Sanitation: All waste from processing poultry which Is found in any open-air area shall be removed within twenty-four (24) hours. Poultry litter shall be ramoved from any enclosure at least once each week. Enclosures must include proper drainage and remain dry, with properly functioning ventilation and drinking systems. Exterior walls, fences, and roofs of enclosures, yards, or processing structures, along with all coops and cages, must remain clean of all waste, stains, or other residue, per Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 40-13-10-.06.

- 4. Litter: Poultry litter that is not being recycied per a nutrient management plan (NMP) or other waste management process approved by the relevant state or federal agency shall be disposed at a sanitary landfill or, alternatively, used or sold for use as organic fertilizer or in some other manner consistent with generally accepted agricultural practices.

(f}) Breeding: Breeding poultry for non-commercial purposes is permitted only to replenish depleted stock up to a maximum of 200 poultry birds. Breeding resulting in more than 200 poultry birds without a commercial poultry permit is prohibited. Breeding poultry for commercial purposes on any property not in the forestry-agriculture district is a separate and distinct violation of the Ordinance.

- (g) No Permit. No permit is required for non-commercial poultry farming.

- (h) inspection: The Administrator is authorized to inspect any property where noncommercial poultry farming is taking place to enforce the provisions of this Ordinance.

(j} Nuisance: A nuisance, as defined in Sec. 2.1, may occur even when there is compliance with other applicable law, including this ordinance. The Administrator may determine what conduct is necessary for abatement of any nuisance, Including but not limited to changing the locations of enclosures and waste storage as well as modifying sanitation practices and schedules. Fallure to abate a nulsance as required by the Administrator may result in penalties and remedies under existing law.
